text:
marta: Quick Q — before I flip the emergency disable for the streaming inference route, want to confirm the exact escalation steps and who is allowed to flip in prod. Also where does the audit entry land?

devon: You can give context: is this for a canary that’s misbehaving or full-prod outage?

marta: Canary (5% traffic). Latency spikes and tail errors. Ops wants a temporary global disable if it keeps spiking.

kevin: Short answer: only members of infra-admins or an approved oncall can run the disable in prod. We try to avoid org-wide kills unless SRE + Platform sign-off.

jordan: Adding process: 1) call in #incidents and ping @oncall, 2) attempt scoped mitigation (canary rollback / reduce audience), 3) if still bad, authorized flip.

marta: Who exactly counts as "authorized flip"? Oncall pager, platform lead, or product owner? Need names/roles so I can call.

kevin: Authorizers are: current pager from eng-oncall rotation, eng-sre lead (or their delegate), and a platform eng with deploy perms. PO only for business-critical decisions; they don't need to flip flags.

devon: Policy excerpt I keep handy: "Feature toggle emergency disable in prod requires two of three: (oncall pager, eng-sre lead, platform lead). Single authorizer allowed only for scoped canary off (<=10% traffic) if risk low."

marta: Good — what about audit? Where does the record show who flipped it and why?

oncall-bot: A record will be created automatically when the toggle API is used. Entry includes actor, flag name, before/after state, reason, and commit id if applicable. Link: https://console.redwood.internal/feature-flags/audit

jordan: In addition, the ops deploy log (deploy-bot) will record any rollout or rollback. For infra-admin console actions we have CloudAudit logs in GCP/AWS depending on cluster.

kevin: Command we use for manual flips (internal):
```
redwood-ffctl toggle --env=prod --flag=streaming_inference_public --action=off --scope=global --actor=kevin --reason="latency tail spike, canary failing"
```
This will create the audit and emit an incident annotation.

marta: If I run that and then later we want to re-enable, what's the guardrail?

devon: Re-enable requires verification that tail errors are fixed and load tested on canary. Prefer staged enable: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 15m observation windows.

jordan: Add automatic safety: if errors > 2x baseline during roll forward, the system auto-pauses and rolls back the percentage.

marta: Good. Where is the escalation contact list? I don't want to hunt Slack history while paging.

kevin: We keep a short rota pinned in the #eng-oncall channel and in the runbook doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/emergency_disable. The pinned one shows current pager + leads and the infra-admins group membership.

marta: Last check — if someone without infra-admins tries the CLI, what happens?

oncall-bot: Attempt blocked. CLI will respond with 403 and guidance: "insufficient privileges — request via /incidents or contact infra-admins". The attempted action is still recorded in audit as a failed attempt.

devon: Also, if someone flips via the web console, we require MFA for users in infra-admins for prod toggles.

marta: Perfect. I'll open the incident channel first and call the pager. If we do need to flip, I'll follow the two-of-three rule and paste the audit link in the thread. Thanks. :thumbsup:

kevin: Thanks — tagging this convo into the runbook as a recent clarifying note. :eyes:

jordan: If you want, leave the exact text of the reason and I'll add a standard template for the audit message so it's consistent.

marta: Copy of reason I'll use: "Canary 5% -> latency p99 3.6s (baseline 0.8s), error rate 1.8% -> 5%. Temporarily disabling streaming_inference_public to protect users and reduce token cost while investigating."

devon: Good language. One more: add any related deploy ids and model hash if toggling due to model regression.

marta: Will do. I’ll update once pager responds.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1842 — channel #incidents-1859123456. Audit link will appear after action.
